questions.question: A current-carrying straight conductor is placed in a magnetic field. The conductor experiences the maximum force when the angle between the direction of the current in it and the direction of the magnetic field is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __90°__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **force** experienced by a** current-carrying conductor **placed in a **magnetic field **is given by the formula **F = BILsinø, **where B is the magnetic field strength, I is the current flowing through the conductor, L is the length of the conductor, and ø is the **angle** between the direction of the current and the direction of the magnetic field.
 
• The **maximum force** is experienced when the angle is **90o**, but in this case, the** sinø **becomes **1,** which is the maximum value.
 
• However, in practical scenarios, it is **not always** possible to have the conductor** perpendicular** to the magnetic field.
 
• When the angle is **0 degrees,** the force experienced is** zero** because sinø is zero.
 
• When the angle is **180 degrees**, the force experienced is** also zero **because sinø is again zero.
 
• Therefore, the maximum force is experienced when the angle between the direction of the current in the conductor and the direction of the magnetic field is 90** degrees** because the sin90 is the maximum value of** 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When the angle between the direction of the current in the conductor and the direction of the magnetic field is** 30 degrees**, the sinø is 0.5, which is **less than** the maximum value of 1.

 
 
• Therefore, the force experienced will be** less than** the maximum force.
 
 
 
• When the angle between the direction of the current in the conductor and the direction of the magnetic field is **60 degrees,** the sinø is 0.866, which is less than the maximum value of 1.
 
 
• Therefore, the force experienced will be **less **than the maximum force.

questions.question: In the absence of atmosphere, the colour of the sky would be:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**black.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The reason behind the** blue colour **of the sky is **Rayleigh scattering**, which occurs due to the **scattering of sunlight** by the molecules in the Earth's atmosphere.
 
• As there is **no atmosphere** in the absence of it, there would be **no scattering of sunlight**, and the sky would appear **black.**
 
• **Red and white colours **are also not possible as they are also the result of scattering of light in the atmosphere, and in the absence of it, the sky would not appear in any colour.
 
• The black colour of the sky would also mean that **stars would appear brighter **and the contrast between them and the sky would be much clearer.
 
• The concept of the sky being black in the absence of atmosphere is also applicable to other** planets and moons** without an atmosphere, such as the Moon and Mercury.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **scattering of light** by particles up to a **tenth of its wavelength** that happen in its path without causing an **energy loss or wavelength change** is known as Rayleigh scattering.
 
• **Red colour** appears during **sunrise and sunset **when the sunlight passes through more atmosphere, scattering the **shorter blue and green** wavelengths and allowing the longer red wavelengths to **pass through.**
 
• **White colour **appears when sunlight is **scattered equally** by all the molecules in the atmosphere, making the sky appear as a bright white.

questions.question: Which of the following elements shows a catenation property like carbon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Si.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Catenation** refers to the ability of an element to **form bonds **with other atoms of the same element, resulting in the formation of **long chains or rings**.
 
• **Carbon** is well known for its **catenation property, **which is why it can form a vast number of organic compounds. 
 
• **Silicon** (Si), shows a catenation property like carbon.
 
• This is because silicon has** four valence electrons**, like carbon, and can form **covalent bonds** with other silicon atoms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Neon** (Ne) **does not** show catenation property as it is a **noble gas** and does not readily form bonds with other atoms.
 
• **Oxygen** (O) can form **limited catenation**, but not to the same extent as carbon or silicon.
 
 
• This is because oxygen has only **two valence electrons** and can only form **two covalent bonds** with other oxygen atoms.
 
 
 
• **Potassium** (K) is a metal and **does not **show catenation property as metals typically** lose electrons** to form positive ions and do not form covalent bonds with other atoms of the same element.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:

(a) The red light has a wavelength about 1.8 times greater than the blue light.

(b) When sunlight passes through the atmosphere, the fine particles scatter blue light more strongly than red.

Which of the above statements help(s) us to understand the blue colour of a clear sky?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Both (a) and (b)**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The statement** (b)** helps us to understand the** blue colour** of a **clear sky.**

 
 
• When sunlight passes through the atmosphere, the fine particles present in the air **scatter blue light **more strongly than red.
 
• This is known as **Rayleigh scattering** and it is the reason why the sky appears blue during the day.
 
 
 
• The wavelength of blue light is** shorter **than that of red light, so it gets scattered more easily by the particles in the air.
 
• The wavelength of red light is **approximately 1.8 times longer than that of blue light.**
 
• Because of this, **blue light which has shorter wavelengths than red is more severely scattered by fine air particles when it travels through the atmosphere.**
 
• The** sky appears blue when the scattered blue light reaches our sight**.
 
 
• The difference in wavelengths between red and blue light is important in other contexts, such as the** formation of rainbows.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When** sunlight is refracted** via **raindrops** and catches an observer's eyes, a **rainbow** is created.
 
• Instead of the frequently portrayed "teardrop" shape, the majority of raindrops are **spherical.**
 
• This spherical form creates the** ideal environment** for the appearance of a rainbow.

Three times the present age of Sujatha is 5 years more than two times the present age of Vanita.

Let the present age of Vanita be V

Let the present age of Sujatha be S

⇒ 3S - 2V = 5 ..(1)

⇒ 3(V + 3) + 4 = 4(S + 3)

⇒ 4S - 3V = 1..(2)

Solving both 1 and 2.

V = 17 and S = 13

According to the question;

V - S = K

k = 17 - 13 = 4 years

**The answer is 4 years.**

questions.question: Two resistors, A (20 Ω) and B (30 Ω), are connected in parallel. The combination is connected to a 3 V battery. The current through the battery is:

__
 
• The** total resistance** in a **parallel circuit** is given by the formula:** 1/Rt = 1/R1 + 1/R2,** where R1 and R2 are the resistances of the two parallel branches.
 
• So, in this case, 1/Rt = 1/20 + 1/30 = **1/12.**
 
• Rearranging the formula, we get **Rt = 12/5 = 2.4 ohms**.
 
• This is the** equivalent resistance** of the parallel combination.
 
• Using Ohm's Law, we can find the current through the battery, which is given by** I = V/Rt, **where V is the voltage of the battery.
 
• In this case, V = 3V, so I = 3/2.4 = **1.25 A.**
 
• However, this is not the final answer because the question asks for the** current **through the battery, not the equivalent resistance.
 
• So, we need to find the** current** through each resistor separately.
 
• Using Ohm's Law again, we can find the current through resistor A, which is I1 = V/R1 = 3/20 = **0.15 A.**
 
• Similarly, the current through resistor B is I2 = V/R2 = 3/30 =** 0.1 A.**
 
• The total current through the battery is the sum of the currents through each resistor, which is I = I1 + I2 = 0.15 + 0.1 = **0.25 A.**
 
• Therefore, 0.25 A is the **correct answer.**

questions.question: An article is marked 50% above its cost price. If the shopkeeper gives two successive discounts of 10% and 25%, and still earns a profit of ₹15, then the cost price of the article is:

An article is marked above the cost price = 50%

Two successive discounts are 10% and 25%

Formula Used: 

Selling Price = Cost Price(1 + Profit%/100)

Marked Price = Cost Price (1 + Marked%/100)

Calculation: 

Let the cost price of an article be 100x 

Marked Price of an article = 100x + 50% of 100x = 150x 

SP = 150x × (9/10)(3/4) = 405/4x

Profit = 405/4x - 100x = 5/4x

5/4x → 15

x = 12

The cost price of the article = 100 × 12

⇒ Rs 1200

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1200.

questions.question:
In which of the following cases does a concave mirror form a real image?

(i) Object placed between focus and pole

(ii) Object placed at infinity

(iii) Object placed at focus
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (ii) and (iii).**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **concave mirror** is a** reflective** surface that **curves inward, **and the **reflecting surface** is on the** inner side **of the curve.
 
• The center of the curve is known as the **focus.**
 
• When an object is placed at the** focus** of a concave mirror, the reflected rays** diverge **and **do not intersect.**
 
• However, if an object is placed **beyond the focus,** the reflected rays** converge** to form a** real image**.
 
• When an object is placed at** infinity, **the reflected rays are **parallel, **and they **converge** at the focus after reflection.
 
• As a result, an **image is formed **at the focus, but it is not a real image.
 
• It is a** virtual image.**
 
• When an object is placed** beyond the focus** of a concave mirror, the reflected rays** converge **to form a real image. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When an object is placed between the** focus and the pole** of a concave mirror, the reflected rays **converge** to form a **real image.**
 
• When an object is placed at the** focus **of a concave mirror, the reflected rays are** parallel,** and they do not converge to form a** real image.** 
 
• A **real image** is formed when the reflected rays converge to a point after reflection.
 
 
• It can be captured on a screen and is always **inverted.**
 
 
 
• A **virtual image** is formed when the reflected rays appear to converge to a point but do not actually do so.
 
 
• It cannot be captured on a screen and is always **upright.**

questions.question: The tendency of formation of basic oxide _____ when we are shifting down in a group.

• A **basic oxide** is formed when an element combines with oxygen and produces a** basic solution** when dissolved in water. 
 
• The trend of basic oxide formation in a group is** dependent** on the** size of the atom** and its** valence electrons.**
 
• As we **move down** a group, the** atomic size increases**, and the valence electrons are located farther from the nucleus.
 
• The increase in atomic size and **distance of valence electrons** from the nucleus leads to a **decrease** in the effective nuclear charge experienced by the valence electrons.
 
• As a result, the valence electrons are **less strongly attracted** to the nucleus, making it easier for them to form a basic oxide.

• As a result, the **atomic radii decreas**e and the** nucleus exerts a stronger attraction** on the outside electrons as one moves from l**eft to right** across a period.
 
• The number of **full electron shells rises** as one moves down a group in the periodic table.
 
• The orbitals of valence electrons in a group are now farther from the nucleus, but they still have the** same effective nuclear charge.**
 
• The atomic radii are therefore** larger** and the** nucleus exerts less force **on the outside electrons.

questions.question: _______ means the additional satisfaction or benefit (utility) that a consumer derives from buying an additional unit of a commodity or service.

• The study of individual and business resource allocation for **production, exchange, and consumption** is known as microeconomics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Consumer Demand and Equilibrium are both **important concepts** in market analysis, as they help explain how prices are determined and how markets function.
 
• **Total Utility** refers to the **total satisfaction or benefit **a consumer gets from consuming a certain quantity of a commodity or service.
 
• Total Utility is also important in understanding **consumer behavior**, as it helps determine the optimal level of consumption for a given commodity or service.
 
• Understanding these concepts is important for** businesses and policymakers** alike, as they can help inform decisions about pricing, production, and regulation.

questions.question: Induced EMF in a coil during the phenomenon of electromagnetic induction is directly proportional to:

The correct answer is __**rate of change in magnetic flux.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Induced EMF** in a coil during the phenomenon of electromagnetic induction is** directly proportional **to the** rate of change in magnetic flux.**
 
• **Electromagnetic induction** is the process of generating an **electromotive force** (EMF) in a conductor by changing the magnetic field around it.
 
• The magnitude of the induced EMF depends on the **rate of change of magnetic flux **through the coil.
 
• This means that the **faster the magnetic field changes,** the **greater the induced EMF** will be.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Magnetic flux** is the amount of **magnetic field** passing through a surface.

 
 
• It is given by the product of the **magnetic field strength** and the **area of the surface perpendicular** to the field.
 
• However, the induced EMF is directly proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux, **not **the magnetic flux itself.
 
 
 
• **Resistance** of the circuit **does not** affect the magnitude of induced EMF.
 
 
• It only affects the **current** flowing through the circuit according to Ohm's Law.
 
 
 
• The phenomenon of electromagnetic induction was discovered by **Michael Faraday in 1831.**
 
• **Faraday's Law of Electromagnetic Induction **states that the EMF induced in a circuit is proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux through it.
 
• The **direction** of induced EMF is given by** Lenz's Law, **which states that the direction of the induced EMF is such that it opposes the change in magnetic flux that produced it.
